blocks.text:
**Build the tools that make a €1.2bn Nordic integration run on less manual reconciliation.**
Kesko has said it targets group net sales of some €20bn in the early 2030s, and it has agreed to acquire Dahl's technical trade operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark. We noticed that Dahl's units keep separate brands, which can mean order and financial data has to be reconciled across units by hand. A 48-hour sprint is a good way to test where that work actually sits.

rows: Order and data flow across units
Cut manual reconciliation of orders and financial data between Kesko units and acquired operations
A working prototype that matches or flags order and ledger records across two units without manual copy-paste
Give integration teams a faster way to onboard acquired operations into shared workflows
A demo that maps one Dahl workflow into a shared process with clear owners and fewer hand-offs
Fill gaps around the new Manhattan ActiveWarehouse rollout in the distribution network
A tool that connects warehouse events to order, invoicing or supplier workflows and surfaces exceptions early

items.text: Build a matching engine that reconciles orders from a technical trade unit against invoices and delivery records, and lists only the exceptions for a human to review.
Create a dashboard for integration leads that tracks which acquired-unit processes are still running on manual steps, week by week, until cutover.
Prototype a supplier onboarding flow for acquired Nordic suppliers that pre-fills master data from existing records and flags duplicates.
Connect warehouse exception events from the new ActiveWarehouse system to customer order status, so a delayed pallet triggers the right update without an email chain.
Automate the pull of tender award records into a single internal view so procurement teams stop checking public notices by hand.
Build a 'first 30 days' checklist agent for a new Dahl site that tracks open data-migration tasks, owners and blockers in one place.
Business impact: would this measurably reduce manual work or cycle time in a real Kesko process?
Feasibility: can it work with the systems and data Kesko already uses, within a realistic integration timeline?
Adoption: would the named process owner use it on Monday, and what would change for their team?
Clarity: is the demo simple enough that a CFO or COO could follow it in five minutes?

blocks.text: Practicalities: the sprint runs for 2 days. Each team has a Velho expert, two builders and Kesko's process owner. The aim is a working demo by Monday, with the process owner able to say what they would use, change or drop.

blocks.label: Cover note to the CEO
blocks.text: Jorma, we wrote you a hackathon brief. It's built around the Dahl integration and the ActiveWarehouse rollout, with six specific prompts your teams could test in 48 hours. We'd like to run it for you: Velho experts and builders alongside a Kesko process owner, with a working demo by Monday. Would a 20-minute call next week be useful to talk through which challenge fits best?
